title: A cache that forgets
description:
Use a weak table so cached values disappear when nothing else uses them.

```
cache size before: 2
dropped one object and collected garbage
cache size after: 1
```

starter.main.lua:
local info = {}

local function count(t)
  local n = 0
  return n
end

local a, b = {}, {}
info[a] = "first"
info[b] = "second"
print("cache size before:", count(info))

hints: Without `__mode = "k"`, the table keeps `b` alive by itself, so it is never collected (lesson 7.02).
`b = nil; collectgarbage(); collectgarbage()` (twice is safest) and then count again.
requirements: `setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })` keys an extra-information table by objects.
Show that an entry vanishes after the object is unreachable and `collectgarbage()` runs.
Write `count(t)` with `pairs`, since `#` does not work here.
stretch: Make a memoize function whose cache uses weak values (`__mode = "v"`).
